feature_request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.

proposed_scope_in.item: Read-only 'Engagement History' tab on the existing Country page, showing existing Engagement records for that country in reverse-chronological order (date, type, contact, linked mission/project, notes summary).

Pre-mission view: on the new-mission creation screen, once a Country is selected, show a read-only link/summary panel (last engagement date, count of engagements in the past 24 months, and a link to the full Country history).
Filters on the history list using existing fields only: date range, engagement type, contact, and linked mission/project; with pagination and CSV-free on-screen viewing.
Access to history inherits the existing Country/Mission permission model: a user sees only the engagement records they could already see today. No new roles or visibility flags are introduced.
History is populated automatically from data already captured (engagements, missions, project affiliations). No new mandatory fields for Regional Coordinators.

proposed_scope_out: Any new data-entry fields or forms for Regional Coordinators (e.g., mandatory outcome ratings, sensitivity tags).
Back-filling or cleaning historical engagement data that was never recorded in the CRM (e.g., paper files, email archives, legacy systems).
AI-generated summaries, scoring, sentiment, or recommendations about a country's relationship.
Per-record or per-country confidentiality classification and new RBAC roles; classification decisions stay with the institution.
Gate or approval workflow that blocks mission creation until history is reviewed or acknowledged.
Cross-country or portfolio-wide history search and analytics dashboards.
Export (CSV/PDF) and printing of the history.
Automatic alerts or notifications about stale contacts or lapsed engagement.

assumptions.statement: 'Full history of engagement' means the engagement records already stored in the CRM (Engagement, Mission, Project affiliation entities), not off-system communications or pre-CRM records.
assumptions.rationale: Reusing existing entities means no new tables and no data migration, so a small team can ship in one release cycle, and Regional Coordinators have nothing extra to enter.

assumptions.statement: Project managers already have permission to view the country and mission records they work on, and the history view can inherit those existing permissions without new access rules.
assumptions.rationale: Inheriting the current Country/Mission access model avoids building a custom RBAC system and keeps the release small, while ensuring users do not see more than they can already see.

assumptions.statement: 'Before starting a new mission' means the history should be surfaced at mission-creation time as an informational aid, not enforced as a required step.
assumptions.rationale: A read-only panel is a simple UI addition; a mandatory review gate would require workflow state, approvals, and exception handling that would not fit in one release.

assumptions.statement: The existing engagement data is recorded consistently enough (date, country, contact, type) to produce a useful chronological view without a cleanup project.
assumptions.rationale: Assuming usable baseline quality lets v1 ship as a view over existing data; gaps are shown as-is rather than blocking launch, and any data quality work is deferred based on real feedback.

success_criteria: A project manager can reach a country's full engagement history in 2 clicks or fewer from the new-mission creation screen.
The history tab loads the first page (up to 50 records) in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile for the country with the largest record count.
Zero new required fields are added to any Regional Coordinator workflow, verified by comparing form schemas before and after release.
Permission test: 100% of test cases confirm a user sees only engagement records they can already access via existing Country/Mission permissions.
Within 60 days of release, at least 50% of new missions have the country history viewed by the creating project manager within 7 days before mission creation, measured via page-view logs.

challenges.challenge_text: A2 assumes project managers' existing permissions are per-country/per-mission and can simply be inherited. But 'full country history' aggregates engagements from every mission, including missions the PM is not assigned to. If today's permission model grants Country-page access broadly (e.g., all PMs can open any Country page) while Engagement records were only visible via the missions they work on, a PM on a trade mission with Country X could now see notes and contacts from a sensitive security or political mission run by another team. The new aggregated view becomes a privilege-escalation path. The proposal states 'sees only records they could already see' but never verifies that engagement-level visibility exists in the current model rather than being implicit via the UI path.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: the Proposer asserts inheritance without evidence that record-level permissions exist for Engagements. The permission test in the success criteria only checks against the existing model, so it would not catch an existing model that is too permissive at aggregate level.

challenges.challenge_text: The history list shows a 'notes summary' and contact names for each engagement. Engagement notes frequently contain candid commentary about ministry officials, negotiating positions, or political context. Surfacing a notes summary in a list view, and in a pre-mission panel on the creation screen, widens exposure: shoulder-surfing, screenshots, and PMs from a different team with only Country-level access see candid notes about named ministry officials. Notes and contact details are the most confidentiality-sensitive fields, yet they are included by default with no field-level restriction.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: the Proposer puts per-record classification out of scope, which is a policy matter, but it still includes the notes summary by default. An engineering option exists: omit notes from the list and show them only on the detail view under the existing permission check, or make the summary opt-in.

challenges.challenge_text: A4 assumes engagement data is consistent enough, but with ~100 countries and frequent turnover of both ministry contacts and Regional Coordinators, engagement records will reference contacts who have since left, been replaced, or been deleted/merged. The history would show a contact name with no indication that the person is no longer in post. A PM could then plan a mission around a former minister or an outdated counterpart, and a wrong ministry contact can damage the relationship. Missing or null contacts or dates would also silently distort the 'last engagement date' and the 24-month count, giving false reassurance that a country is 'recently engaged'.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: the Proposer defers data quality, shows gaps 'as-is', and explicitly excludes stale-contact alerts. There is no handling of contact status or an 'as of' indicator, and no treatment of incomplete records in the summary counts.

challenges.challenge_text: The pre-mission panel shows 'last engagement date' and a 24-month count, with a link to history, but it is purely passive. A PM who sees '12 engagements' may take it as complete coverage, when A1 says off-system and pre-CRM records are excluded and some records are hidden by permissions. A PM with restricted access could see a low or zero count and conclude the country is untouched, then launch a duplicate or conflicting mission while another team's mission is active. The summary counts also may not reflect permission filtering consistently with the list, so count and list could disagree or leak the existence of hidden records.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: the Proposer's summary panel does not state its coverage limits, and no rule defines whether counts are computed over visible records only. Active missions in the same country are not surfaced.

challenges.challenge_text: Success criteria measure speed and page views but there is no audit trail for access to a country's full engagement history. If a contact list or notes leak, there is no way to establish which PM viewed which country's history. The proposal's new aggregated view makes bulk browsing of 100 countries' histories easy, and the cross-country search is out of scope but a PM can still page through every country one by one. On-screen only does not prevent copy/paste.
challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: Round 1: no logging of reads beyond the page-view logs used for adoption metrics, and no stated retention or access to those logs for security review.

challenge_responses.response: The Critic is right that Country-page access may be broader than Engagement visibility. The fix is cheap: the history query reuses the server-side check that already governs opening an Engagement or Mission directly, and does not rely on Country page access. No new roles or tables. The permission test matrix now includes a PM with Country access but no access to a given mission. If the current model has no record-level Engagement visibility, so that the aggregate view would widen exposure, that is a security-clearance and data-classification decision I cannot make. It should be routed to a human before release. I am not inventing a visibility policy.

Removing notes from the list and panel is cheaper than adding field-level controls. Notes now appear only on the existing Engagement detail view under the existing permission check. This removes the highest-sensitivity free text from the aggregated surface and the shoulder-surfing and screenshot exposure on the mission-creation screen. Contact names stay, because the history is not useful without knowing who was engaged. Whether notes need classification-based restriction is an institutional policy matter, and v1 does not decide it.

Staleness is a real risk, but the fix does not need alerts or cleanup. Each contact shows its existing status or last-updated value from the Contact record (A5). Deleted or merged contacts show 'Contact record removed'. The last-date and 24-month count use only dated records, and undated records are shown under an 'Undated' label rather than silently dropped. This is a read-only display over existing data with no new columns, no Regional Coordinator input, and no monitoring queue. Stale-contact alerts and data cleanup stay out of scope. Add them later if post-release feedback shows PMs acting on outdated contacts.

Two cheap fixes address the real harm of false reassurance and mission duplication. The panel and list share one permission-filtered query, so counts cannot disagree with the list. The panel carries a fixed label stating coverage limits (CRM records you can access; excludes off-system and pre-CRM history). The panel also shows the count of currently active missions in that country that the user can see, using the existing Mission status field. I am not adding disclosure of hidden records, because that would leak what permissions are meant to conceal. Whether PMs should learn that hidden active missions exist is a security and diplomatic-policy decision for a human, not a design call.

Basic attribution is already in v1: the page-view log required for the adoption metric records user id, country id, and timestamp for the history tab and Engagement detail (A6), so a leak can be traced to viewers of a given country. What the Critic adds beyond that is an audit viewer, bulk-browsing detection, rate limiting, and retention rules. Those are expensive (a screen or queue someone must watch, plus alerting) and are not justified in v1. Bulk paging is bounded by the record-level permission filter from C1 and the removal of notes from lists (C2). A PM can already open every Country page they have access to today. Copy/paste cannot be prevented in software, and retention and security-review access to logs are institutional decisions for a human. I would add monitoring if a security review finds the logs insufficient or anomalous access patterns appear.

challenges.evaluation_of_proposer: The revision removes the main risk. The history query now reuses the server-side Engagement/Mission visibility check rather than Country-page access. Records the user cannot open are omitted from the list, counts and panel. The release gate includes the key test case, a PM with Country access but no access to a given mission. If the current model has no record-level visibility, the gate will expose that and it becomes a policy decision for the institution, which the Proposer has already said it will route to a human. final_decision.executive_summary: V1 is a read-only view over existing CRM data: notes appear only on the Engagement detail view, every history query applies record-level Engagement/Mission visibility, contacts show their current status, and views are recorded in the existing page-view log. surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C4 (passive panel could give false reassurance or lead to duplicate missions) was revised with a shared permission-filtered query, a coverage-limits label and an active-mission count. The Critic then escalated it to a human, so C4 ended ESCALATED_TO_HUMAN.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The existing engagement data is recorded consistently enough (date, country, contact, type) to produce a useful chronological view without a cleanup project.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: C3 (stale or removed contacts, missing dates distorting counts) was revised with contact status display, a 'Contact record removed' label and an 'Undated' bucket excluded from counts. The Critic accepted it, so C3 ended ACCEPTED.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The existing Contact entity already carries a status or last-updated indicator that can be displayed read-only next to a contact name; if neither exists, the history shows 'status unknown' instead of adding a field.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Added by the Proposer in round 2 to support the C3 fix. No Critic issue targeted it, and it was not challenged.

surfaced_assumptions.assumption: The existing page-view logging (already needed to measure adoption) can record user id, country id, and timestamp for the history tab and Engagement detail views.
surfaced_assumptions.resolution_notes: Added by the Proposer in round 2 to support access logging in response to C5. No Critic issue targeted it directly, and it was not challenged.

open_questions_for_humans.decision_owner: Head of Diplomatic Security (with the Product Owner)
open_questions_for_humans.question: Should a project manager be told that active missions exist in a country that their permissions hide, so they do not launch a duplicate or conflicting mission? Engineering has made the panel count match the permission-filtered list, added a coverage-limits label and an active-mission count the user can see. Whether to disclose hidden missions trades confidentiality against duplicate-mission risk, and engineering cannot make that policy call.

Is the existing page-view log (user id, country id, timestamp) enough as the audit trail for access to country engagement history? If not, what log retention period, tamper-resistance, and security-review access should apply? The Critic escalated these because they are institutional security-governance decisions. V1 deliberately excludes an audit viewer, bulk-browsing detection and rate limiting.
